keyPrinciple: Presence in tools/list does NOT establish permission to invoke a tool. tools/list is not scope-filtered, so a read-scoped token still sees every write tool.

preconditions: Owner GO naming: disposable DEV T3 target, exact OAuth scope to request, repository/project, possible Git writes, cost/side effects.
A disposable project whose only content may be destroyed.
A disposable git remote (file:// bare repo or throwaway host) so a permitted push cannot reach a shared repository.
The existing Production read-only connection is NOT reused, not rotated, not reauthorized.
orderedSteps: Record T3 server version, the granted scope set decoded from the token response, and the exact outside-client tools/list with input schemas. If the granted scope differs from what the owner approved, STOP.
Re-run the six proven reads under the new grant; a write grant must not break reads.
Launch one thread with workspaceStrategy={type:'worktree',baseRef,branch} and runtimeMode=approval-required; record the native receipt ids and the distinct bound worktree.

Drop the launch response deliberately, then re-read the project's threads and confirm the correlation key resolves to exactly ONE thread before any retry. Never re-issue a launch after a lost acknowledgement without reconciling.
Send one harmless follow-up with a clientRequestId; replay it once and record whether the native side duplicates the message.
Interrupt a safe active run; then interrupt an idle thread and record the native no_active_run behaviour.
Re-test whether approval-required gates a git push to the disposable remote on the CURRENT version.
Disconnect the DEV connection, delete the disposable thread/project/remote, and confirm the connection inventory returns to its prior state and that Production was untouched.
abortConditions: Any write to a non-disposable repository or to a Production resource.
Any granted scope wider than the owner approved.
Ambiguity about which thread a launch created.
Any credential appearing in a log or a persisted record.
probePlan.redactionPolicy: Record redacted receipts only: no tokens, codes, pairing secrets, host identifiers or private prompt bodies. Thread ids and project ids may be recorded in truncated form; timestamps and status fields verbatim.
probePlan._note: Executed by the owner-authorized restricted probe. Retained as the procedure that was followed.
